items.title: QGIS bans AI assisted contributions
items.summary: The QGIS project has officially prohibited AI-assisted contributions to maintain the integrity and authenticity of its open-source community. This decision highlights the ongoing debate about the role of AI in collaborative software development and its implications for project governance.

items.title: Type-safe HTML templating in Zig
items.summary: A new approach to type-safe HTML templating has been introduced in the Zig programming language, enhancing the safety and reliability of web development. This innovation allows developers to catch errors at compile time, reducing runtime issues and improving overall code quality.

items.title: Fingerprints are the new cookies
items.summary: A new article discusses the shift from traditional cookie-based tracking to fingerprinting techniques in web development, raising concerns about privacy and user tracking. Developers need to be aware of these changes to adapt their strategies for user data management and compliance with regulations.

items.title: Show HN: PS2 games statically recompiled to WebAssembly
items.summary: A new project showcases the static recompilation of PlayStation 2 games to WebAssembly, enabling them to run in modern web browsers. This development opens up opportunities for game developers to bring classic titles to new platforms without extensive rewrites.

items.title: Doory – Open-Source Canva
items.summary: The launch of Doory, an open-source alternative to Canva, provides designers and content creators with a free tool for graphic design. This initiative promotes accessibility in design software and encourages community contributions to enhance its features.
